A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPTNT benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H are readable and can be matched across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original gameplay experiments with five multimodal models and ten human pairs, alongside offline VQA, localisation, and diagnostic evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a repeated-attempt investigation using Qwen3.5.

M1.justification: The agent roles, asynchronous and synchronous execution, set-of-marks interaction, ReAct outputs, and prompts remain unchanged. The new formal formulation and minimal-harness rationale describe the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same KTANE missions and module types, Manual VQA, Simulator VQA/localisation, and human population. Repeating the existing easiest mission does not introduce new coverage; proposed language and gameplay extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain GPT-5.2, Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3 Flash, Qwen3.5 (27B), and InternVL 3.5 (38B), with the same human and random comparisons. CoELA is added to the related-work comparison table, not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix E.2 expands the reported preliminary temperature conditions from 0.0 to zero and near-zero values up to 0.3. The main benchmark retains temperature 0.6, its model configurations, metrics, and gameplay protocols; the new localisation sample breakdown is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted repeated-attempt robustness check in Section 12 and extends preliminary temperature-sensitivity observations. New Appendix G.11.1 examines clock reading and behavioural responses to urgency using gameplay excerpts already present in v1.

E5.justification: Section 12 newly reports 50 independent Qwen3.5 attempts on mission #1 in asynchronous mode. This is a limited repeated-run investigation, not an increase in repetitions throughout the benchmark; confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: The existing benchmark and appendix result tables retain their values. New results include zero successes and 35 timeouts across the 50 Qwen3.5 attempts, expanded low-temperature looping observations, and the finding that expressed urgency does not noticeably change behaviour in the examined traces.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.1 introduces a substantial formal specification as a decentralised partially observable Markov decision process. It defines states, rewards, action and observation spaces, buffers, and timing dynamics, and gives turn and queue bounds. v1 describes the framework procedurally; its existing seed-diversity mathematics is retained.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a benchmark combining real-time collaborative demands, failure of tested models on full asynchronous missions, and diagnostics examining collaboration and memorisation. The abstract and contribution bullets reframe these objectives without establishing a different central scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 qualifies partner compatibility as a hypothesis requiring further testing given the sample size. Section 8 replaces disengagement language with possible unproductive decision loops. v2 also expands human-comparison limitations, explains the minimal harness, and discusses urgency and rule randomisation.

D1.justification: v2 documents handwritten VQA templates and simulator-derived answers/distractors, adds per-module localisation counts in Table D.5, and explains temperature selection. Appendix F.1 newly discloses ethics approval, consent, compensation, and data handling. These additions document existing experiments rather than establish changed execution.

R1.justification: v2 adds CoELA and Real-Time Reasoning Gym to its research positioning, cites Dec-POMDP foundations, and compares its scheduling with PettingZoo and VizDoom. Harness-related discussion is expanded, while the central positioning around integrated real-time collaboration remains.

P1.justification: There are local rewrites of the abstract, contribution bullets, interpretations, and limitations, plus new formulation and time-pressure subsections. Appendix C is renumbered, but the overall narrative organisation and extensive existing technical and prompt material are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is visually revised, Table 1 gains a CoELA row, and Table D.5 is added. Several figures and tables move or receive shorter captions, including the localisation illustration. The existing experimental plots and gameplay examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer dataset and participant reporting, more cautious interpretations, and the targeted repeated-attempt check improve transparency and evidential calibration. Gains are limited because the main results and broader uncertainty reporting remain unchanged. The new formal specification also introduces a discrepancy: Equation 8 omits the 0.5-second loop delay still documented in Appendix C.4.2.
